  id = {EDN-62},
  title = {\texorpdfstring{\texttt{lgbm-\allowbreak{}basic}}{lgbm-basic} is the candidate model},
  date = {2026-09-30},

  topic = {Modelling Approach, Model Evaluation},
  participants = {@lukas2510},
  decision = {\texttt{lgbm-\allowbreak{}basic} is the candidate that the model card and the report put forward, although \texttt{lgbm-\allowbreak{}extended} has the lower pooled MdAPE.
\texttt{lgbm-\allowbreak{}extended} fails SC-06.
SC-04 is missed by every variant on cars over 20 years and is recorded as missed: the threshold stays, the scope gets no age bound, and the segment stays in the breakdown.},
  rationale = {\emph{Alternatives considered:}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, topsep=2pt]
\item \texttt{lgbm-\allowbreak{}extended} as the candidate, with SC-06 as a known limitation: overrides the criterion the first time it fires.
\item One model for complete requests and the other for partial ones: two models and a routing rule; left open for the deployment milestone.
\item An upper age bound in the scope, or a higher SC-04 threshold: the criterion would pass by removing the rows it fails on.
\end{itemize}
\par
\emph{Why:} With every optional field masked, which is a request carrying only what FR-01 requires, the error of \texttt{lgbm-\allowbreak{}extended} rises to 1.65 times its full-input MdAPE and that of \texttt{lgbm-\allowbreak{}basic} to 1.21 times; the bound is 1.5.
On that request the ranking of the two reverses.
The extended features also make the over-20 segment worse, so they are no remedy for SC-04.},
  ai = {Information seeking, Alternative generation, Alternative assessment, Recommendation},
  response = {Accepted},
  assessment = {Two AI sessions measured SC-06 independently and agreed.
One noticed that the all-masked scenario is a request with only the required fields, on which the ranking reverses.
AI recommended this option and left the serving and scope questions to Lukas.
A failure it had predicted did not reproduce on real data, and it reported that.},
  aievidence = {Claude Code sessions of 2026-09-30 on issues \#37 and \#39.},
